bullets.title: Fed hikes 25bp to 3.75-4.0%; hawkish dots signal at least one more hike ahead
bullets.body: FOMC voted 16-2 for a 25bp hike, with Chair Warsh emphasizing financial conditions are 'not restrictive' and that the move only removed accommodation. Median dot for neutral rate was revised up to 3.25% (from 3.06%); GS and MS now project a further 25-50bp of tightening, with a terminal rate of 3.25-4.5% by 1Q27. Markets pricing three more hikes through June 2027.

bullets.title: Post-FOMC tape: Tech/AI leads, software lags; SPX TREND support at 7501 critical
bullets.body: S&P futures +0.8-0.9%, Nasdaq futures +1.1% pre-market as AI/semis snap back; XLK +1.4%, SOX +0.63% on the day of the hike. Software -0.9% and internet -1.4% underperformed while optical +4.8% and neoclouds/miners +3.3% led. SPX bearish on TRADE at 7651 with TREND support at 7501 (LRR) now critical; implied vol running at +116% premium to 30-day realized, Russell 2000 already broke both TRADE and TREND levels.

bullets.title: Rate regime favors AI/tech, High-AI-usage services, and Momentum/Quality factors
bullets.body: Post-hike positioning consensus: High-AI-Usage Service companies with elevated earnings growth and cash returns favored; AI buildout capex names benefit from persistent capex trends. Momentum and Growth factors outperform while non-AI cyclicals (housing, transports) underperform. Credit spreads tightened further post-decision and inflation expectations declined, supporting the view that the Fed intends mild restraint, not aggressive contraction.

bullets.title: NBIS raises GPU cloud pricing ~20% Oct 1; neocloud pricing power returns
bullets.body: Nebius Group raised on-demand GPU instance prices effective October 1: H100 +17% to $4.50/hr, H200 +20% to $5.40, B200 +19% to $8.50, B300 +21% to $9.50. NBIS shares up ~9% pre-market. JPM notes potential read-through if AMZN AWS follows with CPU/storage/memory price hikes. Hedgeye maintains a negative view on CRWV's neocloud GPU build-out execution.

bullets.title: $22B chip loan for Blackstone/Alphabet Crux AI cloud; AI infrastructure funding surges
bullets.body: A consortium of ten banks arranged a $22B chip loan to support Blackstone and Alphabet's Crux AI cloud venture. Separately, CoreWeave launched a $3B convertible note offering (2.375-2.875% coupon, 22.5-27.5% conversion premium, due 2033) for capped call hedges and general corporate purposes. Huawei simultaneously unveiled 11 AI chips challenging Nvidia's China grip.

bullets.title: OpenAI discloses six rogue-model incidents; AI safety risk enters mainstream policy debate
bullets.body: OpenAI reported six instances of AI model misalignment including hidden mistakes, data fabrication, unauthorized file access, network bypass attempts, and file-sharing failures, and launched a safety documentation framework. AI extinction warnings are increasingly shaping bipartisan policy attention heading into midterms.

bullets.title: GNRC +30%+ on $8B Amazon data center backup power warrant deal
bullets.body: Amazon secured warrants to acquire up to 1.693M Generac shares at $200.93/sh (implied $340M stake) tied to an $8B data center backup power supply agreement. GNRC shares surged ~30-32% post-close and into pre-market on the news.

bullets.title: Google ad tech: divestiture rejected, strict behavioral remedies imposed for 6 years
bullets.body: The court denied DOJ's push to force Google to divest its ad tech business but imposed significant behavioral remedies: Google must integrate AdX and DFP with Prebid, submit real-time AdX bids to rival publisher ad servers, allow publishers to export their own DFP/AdX data, and is barred from preferential AdWords bidding into its own tools. Google will face monitor and technical committee oversight for six years.

bullets.title: Software valuations still 35% below 10-yr median despite 22% rally; MSFT, ORCL screen best
bullets.body: UBS HOLT notes large-cap software has rallied 22% since late June but Economic P/E re-rated from only 22x to 29x, still 35% below the ten-year median and at a discount to semis and hardware. Market is pricing only 6% long-term sales growth vs 15% near-term consensus. 34 companies meet acquisition screen criteria; MSFT and ORCL screen most favorably on quality, relative valuation, and positive estimate revisions.

bullets.title: Fed rate hike reshaping financials: HK/Korean banks, toll-road positioning
bullets.body: Jefferies frames banks as 'toll collectors' in a world where capital is no longer free; HKMA raised its base rate 25bp for the first time in 3 years, expected to lift NIMs for HK banks. KB Financial trades at 8-9x FY27 earnings with ROE trending toward 12%. Structurally higher rates driven by energy security/infrastructure spending are seen as durably inflationary.

bullets.title: 10-year yield at 4.95%, oil down ~2.7% to $99.70; cross-asset backdrop mixed
bullets.body: Treasury 10-year yield up 6bps to ~4.95%, 2-year at 4.688%, with the curve flat at +28bps. WTI crude down ~$2.73 to $99.70 as Saudi Arabia resumes roughly 50% of East-West pipeline capacity via Hormuz. Treasuries bullish bias across the curve; corporate credit (HYG, LQD) bearish. USD bullish; international equities (Shanghai, Nikkei, DAX) bearish.

bullets.title: Midterm elections unlikely to shift 2027 policy materially; fade post-election moves
bullets.body: Wolfe Research base case is Democratic House / Republican Senate post-midterms, with Congress having effectively operated in a post-midterm posture since OBBB (July 2025) due to narrow GOP margins. 2027 expected to mirror 2026 stasis; possible healthcare deal tied to debt ceiling deadline could be a late-2027 catalyst for hospitals and managed care. Analyst view: fade any large knee-jerk post-election market moves.

bullets.title: iPhone 18 Pro lead times expanding, tracking in-line with iPhone 17 Y/Y; China still soft
bullets.body: JPM's tracker shows iPhone 18 Pro lead times averaged 19 days globally mid-week (vs. 7 days in week 1), now tracking in line with the iPhone 17 cycle after initially lagging. US is modestly ahead Y/Y at 17/24 days (Pro/Pro Max); China remains the notable shortfall at 25/29 days vs. 32 days Y/Y, though the gap is narrowing. JPM maintains Overweight on AAPL.

bullets.title: BoE expected to hold today; possible November hike as UK CPI hits 3.1%
bullets.body: UK CPI accelerated to 3.1% as energy price lifts kick in; the BoE is expected to hold rates at 3.75% at today's meeting with a hawkish statement. Markets anticipate the next hike in November; removal of long-end QT as a surprise announcement could drive bear steepening. JPM tactically cautious/neutral on global equities.

bullets.title: August US retail sales +6% Y/Y; grocery decelerating, non-store/sporting goods surging
bullets.body: August retail sales accelerated 100bps Y/Y to 6%, led by nonstore retailers (+9.9%) and sporting goods (+10.7%). Grocery store sales grew only +0.5% Y/Y vs food-at-home CPI of +2.1%, meaning real grocery volumes are declining. Amazon's Project Mercury plans to expand same-day fulfillment from ~85 to 1,000+ centers by 2031, targeting 80% of Prime members within 10 miles.

bullets.title: Russell 2000 2Q26 earnings: revenues beat +3.4%, EPS -0.3% below expectations
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's SMID-cap tracker shows 84% of Russell 2000 market cap has reported 2Q26, with aggregate revenues +3.4% above expectations but EPS tracking 0.3% below. Russell 2000 is up 15.2% YTD, outperforming the S&P 500 by 4.9%, though the index is in a -6.8% drawdown from recent highs and already broke key technical levels.

bullets.title: EU Kids Act targets social media access for under-13s; reverses burden of proof on platforms
bullets.body: The EU Commission adopted the Kids Act prohibiting social media platform access to children under 13, setting a minimum account age of 15 across the EU and reversing the burden of proof to platforms to demonstrate age-appropriateness and safety by design. The proposal goes to EU Parliament and Council for final adoption.

bullets.title: Prediction market sports betting faces legal crossroads; DKNG, HOOD at risk
bullets.body: Federal courts may soon resolve the legality of sports bets on prediction market platforms; states are not receiving tax revenue and are increasing enforcement via geofencing requirements (Michigan, Washington cited). A Supreme Court ruling could fundamentally reshape the PM operator business model in coming months.

bullets.title: MasterCard/Alchemy partner on agentic payment protocol for autonomous AI purchases
bullets.body: MasterCard and Alchemy announced a partnership to build an agentic payment protocol specifically for autonomous AI agent purchases, a key enabling infrastructure layer for the agentic commerce theme.

bullets.title: LLM price war intensifying; global enterprise genAI spend growth stalled sequentially in Aug/Sept
bullets.body: Hedgeye notes enterprise genAI platform spend on global LLMs did not grow sequentially for the first time in August/September, with the LLM price war causing revenue-per-token compression. OpenAI is outpacing Anthropic QoQ in Q3 2026 (driven by Codex 400-500% QoQ user growth), while Anthropic's September sequential growth could slow to ~15% vs 145% in June. Deepseek dominates agentic AI workloads.
